result.summary: The pedestrian environment features basic sidewalks but lacks essential crossing infrastructure such as marked crosswalks or pedestrian signals at the intersection. The roadway surface is in poor condition, and parked vehicles near the corner create visual obstructions for those attempting to cross.

hazards.name: Unmarked Crossing
hazards.description: There are no painted crosswalks at the intersection, leaving pedestrians without a designated or protected space to cross.

hazards.name: Lack of Pedestrian Signals
hazards.description: While vehicle traffic lights are present, there are no visible pedestrian signal heads to indicate safe crossing times.
hazards.location_in_image: Left side of the intersection on the signal pole

hazards.name: Visual Obstructions
hazards.description: Parked cars along the curb line near the intersection block sight lines between drivers and pedestrians.
hazards.location_in_image: Left side of the street along the curb

hazards.name: Degraded Pavement
hazards.description: The roadway surface is cracked and uneven, which can pose a tripping hazard or affect vehicle control.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Install zebra or ladder-style crosswalk markings to clearly define pedestrian right-of-way.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Signal Heads
interventions.description: Add pedestrian signals with countdown timers to the existing traffic light infrastructure.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions (Bulb-outs)
interventions.description: Construct curb extensions to shorten the crossing distance and prevent parking too close to the intersection, improving visibility.

interventions.title: Roadway Resurfacing
interventions.description: Repair and resurface the intersection to provide a smooth, predictable surface for all users.
